Chapter 1: A Simple Life, A Hidden Treasure
There’s something magical about stories that start in those quiet, overlooked corners of the world—don’t you think? Where hope and ambition quietly simmer beneath the surface of everyday life.
Picture this: in a bustling ancient city, surrounded by noise and chaos, a young man named Hafid worked as a humble camel boy. Day in and day out, he faced dust, sweat, and the same small tasks over and over. Hafid watched life from the sidelines, wishing for something more, but not really sure how to reach it.
The city’s marketplace was alive with energy—merchants shouting deals, coins clinking, fortunes rising and falling in an instant. And right in the middle of it all, Hafid’s world was shaped by his employer, a seasoned trader who’d seen it all: the highs of success, and the lows of disappointment.
This mentor wasn’t just respected for his wealth—he was admired for his integrity, for the way he treated everyone around him. Hafid looked up to him, not just because he was smart in business, but because he seemed to be guided by something deeper—a real sense of purpose.
One evening, as the sun slipped behind the city walls, Hafid found the courage to open up. He shared his dreams with his mentor—how he wanted to rise above his humble beginnings, become a great salesman, and leave his mark on the world. The older man listened closely, his eyes showing both understanding and a hint of challenge.
He explained that true greatness—whether in sales or anything else—doesn’t come from clever words or pure luck. It runs deeper than that. It’s something anyone can learn and practice.
Most people, he said, are always looking for shortcuts or quick wins. They think success is just for the lucky or the naturally gifted. But here’s something to pay attention to: lasting achievement comes from building the right habits, shaping your character a little bit every single day.
Then, almost as if sharing a secret, the mentor hinted at a set of ancient scrolls. Each one held a principle—something powerful enough to turn an ordinary life into something extraordinary.
Hafid’s curiosity was on fire. He could sense these scrolls weren’t just about business—they offered a way to live with real purpose, to find meaning in every action. Sensing this eagerness, the mentor decided to put Hafid to the test. He handed him a small sum of money and a simple robe, asking him to travel to a far-off village and sell it.
It sounded simple, but it was a real test of patience, courage, and faith.
The journey was anything but easy. Hafid faced rejection, self-doubt, and the sting of failure. Door after door closed. Faces turned away. As night crept in, disappointment weighed heavy on his shoulders.
But in a quiet moment, Hafid remembered his mentor’s advice—don’t give up at the first sign of trouble. Keep going. Stay persistent.
Eventually, Hafid’s kindness and sincerity caught the eye of a struggling family. Instead of pushing for a sale, he offered the robe as an act of compassion. And in that moment, it clicked—true selling isn’t about convincing someone or making a quick deal. It’s about serving others, meeting real needs.
The family’s gratitude filled Hafid with a sense of fulfillment that went way beyond money.
When he returned to the city, Hafid shared his story with his mentor. The older man smiled, knowing Hafid had passed the first big test—not by making a sale, but by discovering what it really means to serve.
Suddenly, the road ahead was clear. This wasn’t just about learning techniques, but about changing from the inside out.
That’s when the mentor finally handed Hafid the ancient scrolls—each one a guide to a new way of living. The promise was simple: read each scroll every day, let its wisdom soak in, and let it shape every thought and action you take.
So, here’s the real lesson Hafid learned: greatness isn’t a secret reserved for the lucky few. It’s open to anyone willing to put in the daily work of mastering themselves, one habit at a time.
